operation.reason: ENGINE_GAP: legacy issues one independent GET request per calendar day between start_date and end_date (the date query param IS the loop variable, not a next-page/cursor token); the dialect's pagination types all advance from response state, incremental issues exactly one request per read with a server-side lower-bound filter, and fan_out requires a discoverable/configured id list -- none can express 'N independent single-day requests over a client-computed date range'. See docs.md Known limits.
operation.notes: named_dependency=engine.direct_read_executor: the direct-read executor has no non-redacting output policy for this provider operation

operation.reason: ENGINE_GAP: zips 3 parallel [timestamp,value] arrays (prices/market_caps/total_volumes) into one record per timestamp; the dialect has no array-zip/parallel-array-join primitive. See docs.md Known limits.

operation.reason: ENGINE_GAP: response is a bare array of [timestamp, open, high, low, close] tuples (a JSON array, not an object) per array element; connsdk.RecordsAt's []any case only keeps elements that decode as map[string]any, so a bare-tuple array element is silently dropped, yielding zero records -- the identical root-cause limitation as market_chart's array-zip gap (no array-of-arrays/tuple-to-record primitive), confirmed in this pass rather than assumed. See docs.md Known limits.
operation.notes: named_dependency=engine.direct_read_executor: the direct-read executor has no non-redacting output policy for this provider operation
